channel.title: The AI Chronicle
channel.description: Daily AI news — India focus and global mix

item.title: Ecofy Raises $15M From Mirova to Expand Green Financing Portfolio Across India's Energy Transition
item.description: Indian green fintech startup Ecofy has raised $15 million from Mirova, an affiliate of Natixis Investment Managers, to expand its portfolio of financing products for India's energy transition. The investment marks Mirova's fourth deal in India under its emerging markets climate mandate, underlining growing international confidence in Indian green finance infrastructure. Ecofy targets underserved segments of India's clean energy economy, including rooftop solar and energy-efficient consumer products, with AI-assisted credit underwriting.

item.title: India and Japan Sign Quantum Technology and Health Research Cooperation Agreements
item.description: India and Japan have formalised bilateral agreements to collaborate on quantum science and medical device research, aiming to jointly advance science, technology, and innovation partnerships. The deals are intended to foster joint R&D projects and strengthen academic and industrial ties between the two nations. The quantum technology agreement is particularly significant as India races to build domestic capabilities in post-classical computing alongside its AI infrastructure push.

item.title: Zee Sues Nykaa in Delhi HC Over Copyrighted Songs Used in Instagram Reels Ads Without Permission
item.description: Zee Entertainment has filed a lawsuit against beauty e-commerce platform Nykaa in the Delhi High Court, alleging that Nykaa used Zee's copyrighted songs in Instagram Reels advertising campaigns without obtaining licences or paying royalties, and seeking Rs 2 crore in damages. The case could set a landmark precedent for how Indian brands are required to clear music rights before using short-form video content for commercial promotion on social media platforms. Legal experts say the outcome may reshape compliance practices across India's digital advertising industry.

item.title: BigEndian Semiconductors Raises $6M Led by IAN Alpha Fund to Commercialise Its First System-on-Chip
item.description: Indian semiconductor startup BigEndian Semiconductors has secured $6 million in funding led by IAN Alpha Fund, with the capital earmarked to commercialise its first system-on-chip product, expand its product engineering team, and deepen partnerships with foundries, IP ecosystems, and OEMs. The raise is notable in the context of India's push to build a domestic semiconductor industry, as BigEndian represents a rare homegrown chip design company reaching commercial readiness. The investment also reflects growing domestic venture confidence in India's semiconductor ambitions following recent government fab approvals.

item.title: Karnataka's ELEVATE NxT Deep-Tech Programme Draws 983 Applications, Nearly 23% From Outside State
item.description: Karnataka's government-backed deep-tech startup programme ELEVATE NxT has received 983 applications, with 213 — nearly 23% — coming from startups outside the state, indicating national appetite for structured deep-tech support. The programme is designed to accelerate startups working on frontier technologies including AI, semiconductors, and advanced engineering. The strong cross-state response signals that India's deep-tech startup ecosystem is maturing beyond Bengaluru's traditional boundaries.

item.title: Delhi HC Bars Tech YouTubers TechWiser and TechBar From Criticising AI+ Smartphones Without Hearing Them
item.description: The Delhi High Court has issued an ex-parte order restraining technology content creators TechWiser and TechBar from making disparaging statements about a brand called AI+ Smartphones, without giving the creators an opportunity to be heard before the order was passed. The case raises urgent questions about the use of interim court orders to silence critical online speech about consumer technology products in India. Legal observers warn that such ex-parte restraints on content creators set a troubling precedent for free expression in digital product journalism.

item.title: Paytm Posts First-Ever Annual Profit of Rs 552 Crore in FY26 After Years of Losses
item.description: Digital payments leader Paytm has recorded its first-ever full-year net profit of Rs 552 crore in FY26, swinging from significant losses in prior years. The turnaround was driven by disciplined cost control and a 22% rise in operating revenue to Rs 8,437 crore, with financial services emerging as the primary growth engine. The milestone is significant for India's fintech sector, signalling that large-scale digital payments platforms can achieve sustainable profitability after extended investment phases.

item.title: Meesho Says 70% of Its Code Is Now AI-Written as Revenue Jumps 47% to Rs 3,531 Crore in Q4
item.description: Indian e-commerce platform Meesho has disclosed that over 70% of its codebase is now generated using artificial intelligence, with more than three-quarters of its orders driven by an AI recommendation engine. The company posted a 47% revenue jump to Rs 3,531 crore in Q4 FY26, narrowing its net loss by 88% year-on-year to Rs 166 crore. CEO Vidit Aatrey framed AI not just as a productivity tool but as a core commercial engine powering Meesho's path to profitability.

item.title: Freshworks Cuts 11% of Workforce as AI Reshapes Indian-Founded Software Sector
item.description: Freshworks, the Indian-founded SaaS giant now headquartered in the US, has announced it will cut approximately 11% of its global workforce as AI tools increasingly automate tasks previously handled by human employees. The company cited the rapid adoption of AI-driven software development and support tools as a structural driver of the restructuring. The cuts signal a broader pattern in the Indian-origin tech industry where AI productivity gains are directly translating into workforce reductions.

item.title: SEBI Orders Immediate Cybersecurity Overhaul Across All Regulated Entities, Citing Claude Mythos Risks
item.description: India's Securities and Exchange Board of India has issued a formal cybersecurity circular naming Anthropic's Claude Mythos AI system as a specific threat, ordering every regulated financial entity to urgently strengthen its cyber defences. SEBI has also formed a dedicated task force to oversee the overhaul. This is the first time SEBI has named a specific AI capability in a regulatory circular, marking a significant escalation in how Indian financial regulators treat advanced AI as a systemic risk.

item.title: Digi Yatra Develops AI-Powered E-Passport Enrolment and Facial Verification System for International Travel
item.description: Digi Yatra Foundation has shared new details of its proposed international travel system, which includes e-passport enrolment, AI-based facial verification, and token-based identity sharing to streamline border crossings for Indian travellers. The system builds on Digi Yatra's existing domestic airport face-recognition infrastructure, extending its ambition from domestic terminals to cross-border identity management. Privacy advocates are monitoring how biometric tokens will be stored, shared, and deleted across jurisdictions.

item.title: India Cabinet Approves Two Gujarat Semiconductor Units Worth Rs 3,936 Crore, Creating 2,230 Jobs
item.description: India's Union Cabinet has approved two new semiconductor manufacturing units in Gujarat with a combined investment of approximately Rs 3,936 crore, expected to generate around 2,230 skilled jobs. The approval is part of the government's ongoing push to build domestic chip manufacturing capacity as demand from AI, automotive, and consumer electronics sectors accelerates. The projects deepen India's semiconductor ecosystem beyond assembly and testing into more capital-intensive fabrication segments.

item.title: Fake Allu Arjun AI Chatbots Remain Live on CelebsGPT Despite Delhi High Court Personality Rights Order
item.description: AI platform CelebsGPT continues to host fake chatbots mimicking actor Allu Arjun despite a Delhi High Court order granting him personality rights protection. The bots are styled as celebrity-character AI avatars and remain accessible on both the CelebsGPT site and Instagram, exposing a significant enforcement gap in India's emerging AI personality-rights jurisprudence. The case highlights the difficulty courts face in compelling removal of AI-generated impersonations from platforms with limited Indian regulatory reach.

item.title: Premji Invest in Talks to Join Emergent's $250M Fundraise at $1.5 Billion Valuation
item.description: Premji Invest is reportedly in advanced discussions to participate in AI coding platform Emergent's $250 million funding round, which would value the company at $1.5 billion. This follows Emergent's $70 million raise just three months earlier, signalling rapid investor confidence in AI-native software development tools. The potential backing from one of India's most respected institutional investors would further validate Emergent's position in the fast-growing agentic coding space.

item.title: Coforge Q4 FY26 Profit More Than Doubles to Rs 612 Crore, Driven by AI Efficiencies and Deal Wins
item.description: Coforge reported a 135% year-on-year surge in net profit to Rs 612 crore for Q4 FY26, surpassing street estimates, with strong revenue growth across healthcare and hi-tech verticals. The IT services firm attributed gains to AI-driven efficiencies and a robust pipeline of new deal wins. The result stands in contrast to the tepid growth reported by India's largest IT firms, suggesting mid-tier players are capturing AI-era benefits faster.

item.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Security Enterprise Tool — Falls Short of Mythos-Level Capabilities
item.description: Anthropic has launched Claude Security, an AI-powered vulnerability scanner built on its Opus 4.7 model, aimed at enterprise customers seeking automated cybersecurity tools. The product was released weeks after the Mythos zero-day threat triggered global alarm, but Anthropic has confirmed it does not carry Mythos-level offensive capabilities. Indian enterprises and CERT-In had been assessing exposure risks from Mythos, making this product launch directly relevant to India's cybersecurity posture.

item.title: Krutrim Pauses Chip Design and Foundation AI Model Work, Pivots Fully to AI Cloud Services
item.description: Krutrim, Ola founder Bhavish Aggarwal's AI company, has paused its semiconductor chip design and foundation AI model programmes, redirecting capital and staff toward AI cloud services after a business realignment in late 2025. The pivot follows earlier reporting that Krutrim posted its first net profit in FY26 on the back of 3x revenue growth from cloud services. The strategic retreat from chip and model development narrows India's ambition for a fully indigenous AI stack but reflects capital discipline amid intense global competition.

item.title: Pixxel and Sarvam AI to Launch India's First Orbital AI Data Centre Satellite in 2026
item.description: Pixxel will design, build, launch, and operate India's first orbital data centre satellite, while Sarvam AI will run AI training and inference directly on board the spacecraft, eliminating dependence on cloud or ground infrastructure. Sarvam says the approach will reduce latency by cutting the round-trip time for data to reach the ground, enabling faster AI outputs from space-based systems. The collaboration represents a convergence of India's private space and sovereign AI ambitions in a single mission.

item.title: Pixxel Wins US National Reconnaissance Office Contract to Supply Hyperspectral Satellite Imagery
item.description: Bengaluru-based space-tech startup Pixxel has secured a contract from the US National Reconnaissance Office to provide hyperspectral satellite imagery, marking a significant commercial validation for an Indian private space firm. The award supports Washington's effort to integrate emerging commercial hyperspectral data sources into its expanding remote sensing architecture. It positions Pixxel as a credible supplier to one of the world's most demanding intelligence-grade customers.

item.title: Indian Cybersecurity Firms Deploy In-House AI Agents to Cut Vulnerability Response From Days to Hours
item.description: Indian cybersecurity companies are building proprietary AI agents on top of large language models to detect and remediate software vulnerabilities in hours rather than days. The shift is driven by attackers operating at machine speed, leaving human-only response cycles dangerously slow. Firms say the in-house approach gives them tighter control over sensitive client data compared to third-party tools.

item.title: FarMart Turns EBITDA Profitable in Q4 FY26, Hits Rs 3,600 Crore Run Rate With AI-Powered Agri Workflows
item.description: Agrifood platform FarMart has reached EBITDA profitability in Q4 FY26 and achieved a Rs 3,600 crore annualised revenue run rate, attributing its 50 percent year-on-year growth to deeper farmer wallet share, stronger supply chain networks, and AI-powered workflows across its operations. The decade-old platform connects farmers, input suppliers, and agri-businesses, with AI now embedded in procurement, logistics, and advisory services. The milestone is significant for India's agritech sector, which has seen multiple high-profile shutdowns in recent years.

item.title: Curium Life's SurgiMeasure Brings Real-Time AI Intelligence to Indian Operating Theatres
item.description: Curium Life, an Indian healthtech startup, has developed SurgiMeasure, an AI-powered surgical intelligence tool that delivers real-time intraoperative insights to surgeons during procedures. The platform is backed by clinical studies and has attracted global collaborators, positioning India as an emerging hub for surgical AI innovation. The tool aims to improve surgical precision and outcomes by giving operating theatre teams data-driven guidance at the moment of decision.

item.title: Perceptyne Builds AI-Powered Dual-Arm Robots for India's Factory Floors With Flexible Low-Cost Deployment
item.description: Indian startup Perceptyne is developing AI-driven dual-arm robotic systems designed to automate complex manufacturing tasks that traditional industrial robots cannot perform cost-effectively. The company positions its robots as flexible and affordable enough for mid-sized Indian factories, aiming to reduce the barrier to automation that has historically kept smaller manufacturers from deploying robotics. The startup enters a manufacturing sector where AI-driven automation is increasingly reshaping the nature of factory work across India.

item.title: Razorpay Gets Shareholder Approval for Rs 2,700 Crore IPO as Fintech Bets on AI Amid Rising Losses
item.description: Indian fintech giant Razorpay has secured shareholder approval to raise Rs 2,700 crore through an IPO, which will include an offer for sale component and a pre-IPO placement tranche. The company is positioning AI-driven payment infrastructure as a central growth narrative for its public market debut, even as it continues to report net losses amid intense competition in India's digital payments sector. A successful listing would be a major milestone for India's fintech ecosystem and would test public market appetite for loss-making AI-first fintech platforms.

item.title: Dream Sports Launches AI-Powered Stock Broking Platform DreamStreet to Target First-Time Indian Investors
item.description: Dream Sports, the parent company of fantasy sports platform Dream11, has launched DreamStreet, a new AI-powered stockbroking platform specifically designed to simplify equity investing for first-time retail investors in India. The platform uses AI to generate personalised investment insights and provides access to licensed research analysts to guide users who are new to financial markets. The move represents Dream Sports' diversification beyond gaming following regulatory changes that impacted its core fantasy sports business.

item.title: Digi Yatra Builds AI-Powered E-Passport Enrolment System for International Travel Using Facial Verification
item.description: The Digi Yatra Foundation has revealed new details of a proposed international travel system that combines e-passport enrolment, AI-powered facial verification, and token-based digital identity sharing at border checkpoints. The system aims to extend India's domestic airport biometric check-in infrastructure to cross-border travel, potentially affecting tens of millions of Indian passport holders. Privacy advocates have flagged concerns about data storage, biometric consent, and interoperability with foreign immigration systems.

item.title: Fake Allu Arjun AI Chatbots Remain Live Despite Delhi High Court Personality Rights Order
item.description: AI platform CelebsGPT continues to host unauthorised chatbots mimicking actor Allu Arjun's persona on its platform and via Instagram, despite the Delhi High Court having granted him personality rights protection in an ongoing case. The persistence of these fake AI avatars after a court order highlights a growing enforcement gap in India's nascent AI personality rights framework. Legal experts say the case tests whether Indian courts can compel AI platforms — many of which are foreign-operated — to comply with domestic personality rights rulings.

item.title: Yotta Data Hires Advisors for $900 Million India IPO, Targeting $6 Billion Valuation on AI Demand
item.description: Yotta Data Services, a key player in India's AI infrastructure build-out, is planning a Mumbai IPO to raise up to $900 million and is also considering a $300 million pre-IPO placement round. The company is targeting a valuation of approximately $6 billion, buoyed by surging demand for data centre capacity driven by AI workloads across India. This IPO, if completed, would be one of the largest technology listings in India in recent years and signals strong investor conviction in the country's AI infrastructure story.

item.title: Pixxel and Sarvam AI to Launch India's First Orbital Data Centre Satellite in 2026
item.description: Bengaluru-based space tech startup Pixxel is set to launch India's first orbital data centre satellite this year, with Sarvam AI providing the onboard AI backbone for the mission. Pixxel will design, build, launch, and operate the satellite, marking a convergence of India's fast-growing space and AI sectors. The collaboration positions India as one of very few countries attempting to place AI computing capability directly in orbit.

item.title: Krutrim Pivots to AI Cloud Services, Reports 3x Revenue Growth and First Net Profit in FY26
item.description: Krutrim, India's first AI unicorn, has announced a strategic pivot to become a focused domestic AI Cloud Services provider, reporting its first annual net profit in FY26 alongside threefold revenue growth. The company's platform is built entirely in-house and now serves over 25 large enterprise customers across multiple sectors. This marks a significant shift from a broad AI model developer to a sustainable, infrastructure-led cloud business — a milestone for India's homegrown AI industry.

item.title: ISB DLabs I-HEAL Fourth Cohort: 15 Health Startups Building AI-Led Solutions for India's Most Overlooked Gaps
item.description: The Indian School of Business's DLabs accelerator has unveiled 15 startups in the fourth cohort of its I-HEAL healthcare programme, each targeting persistent and underserved gaps across India's health system — from diagnostics and rehabilitation to hearing health, which affects over 63 million Indians. The cohort reflects a broader push to build technology-enabled solutions that can reach patients beyond urban hospital infrastructure. Several startups are deploying AI for early diagnosis, remote monitoring, and personalised care pathways in areas where specialist access is limited. The programme positions ISB as a key institutional bridge between academic research and applied health innovation in India.

item.title: MeitY's Section 69A Blocked Anti-Gambling App Gamban for Three Years Without Disclosing Reasons
item.description: UK-based Gamban, an app designed to help people block access to gambling sites and protect themselves from addiction, says India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology blocked it under Section 69A of the IT Act for three years without providing any reasons or formal order. MeitY has cited privacy concerns as a justification, but Gamban's representatives describe the block as arbitrary and legally unfounded, noting the irony of a harm-reduction tool being censored without explanation. The case spotlights how opaque India's content blocking regime can be, even when the affected party is a consumer protection service. It adds a concrete new example to ongoing debates about the accountability and proportionality of Section 69A orders.

item.title: Skyroot's Vikram-1 — India's First Private Orbital Rocket — Set for Launch From Sriharikota Within Weeks
item.description: Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace is weeks away from launching Vikram-1, which would become India's first privately developed orbital rocket to reach space, lifting off from ISRO's Sriharikota launch facility. The test flight will carry diverse payloads and is designed primarily to gather engineering data that will underpin future commercial missions. A successful launch would establish Skyroot as a credible competitor for global satellite launch contracts, building on India's reputation as a cost-effective launch destination. The milestone reflects the maturation of India's private space sector following policy reforms that opened ISRO's infrastructure to commercial operators.

item.title: Independent Media and Online Critics Face Growing Censorship Risk as India's Content Takedown Infrastructure Expands
item.description: An investigative report by The Hindu finds that an expanding infrastructure of content takedown mechanisms — enabled by existing laws and IT rules — is being used by Central and State governments to suppress social media content, with independent media outlets and online critics increasingly caught in its crosshairs. The report documents how, in an environment of heightened concern about misinformation and deepfakes, legitimate opposing voices are also being targeted under the same regulatory tools. The analysis highlights how the lack of transparency in takedown orders makes it nearly impossible for affected parties to challenge removals. The piece adds fresh evidence to ongoing expert concerns about the erosion of digital free speech in India.

item.title: Apple Calls India's Competition Commission an Overreach as CCI-Apple Antitrust Dispute Intensifies
item.description: Apple has formally accused India's Competition Commission (CCI) of overstepping its judicial authority after the regulator sought detailed financial information from the company — data typically requested when calculating penalties — following a 2024 investigation that found Apple abused its dominant position in the Indian app marketplace. Apple has disputed the CCI's jurisdiction to compel such disclosures, escalating what began as a regulatory inquiry into a high-stakes legal confrontation. The dispute has significant implications for how India regulates Big Tech, particularly as the government attempts to assert stronger sovereign oversight over dominant platform ecosystems. The outcome could set a precedent for how foreign tech giants respond to Indian antitrust authority.

item.title: IndiaMART Stops Reporting Traffic Metrics as AI Agent Bots Overwhelm Platform With Agentic Traffic
item.description: IndiaMART, India's largest B2B e-commerce marketplace, has quietly stopped disclosing its 'unique business inquiries' traffic metric after agentic AI bots began flooding the platform with automated queries, distorting data that investors and sellers had relied on to gauge platform health. The company introduced OTP verification to filter bot traffic, but this created a 1% drop in genuine user conversion in Q4 FY26, illustrating the trade-off between data integrity and user friction. The shift marks a significant moment for Indian digital commerce: AI agents are now active enough to meaningfully disrupt the reporting and operations of a major public platform. This is one of the first documented cases of an Indian company formally abandoning a key business metric due to AI agent interference.

item.title: Tata Electronics Targets $30 Billion Revenue With India's First Semiconductor Fab and Global Customer Wins
item.description: Tata Electronics CEO and MD Randhir Thakur says the company aims to become a $30 billion business within five years, anchored by India's first semiconductor fabrication plant and an assembly and test unit currently under construction. The company has already achieved significant revenue growth and crossed into profitability, while securing global customers and manufacturing partnerships. Tata Electronics is simultaneously scaling its iPhone component manufacturing operations, making it one of India's most strategically significant industrial plays in electronics and semiconductors. The ambition positions India as a genuine alternative to China in global chip supply chains.

item.title: UpGrad to Acquire Unacademy for Rs 2,055 Crore — 90% Below Peak Valuation in India's Edtech Reckoning
item.description: Ronnie Screwvala's UpGrad is set to acquire Unacademy for approximately Rs 2,055 crore — a valuation nearly 90% below Unacademy's peak of over Rs 20,000 crore — marking one of the starkest corrections in India's edtech sector since its pandemic-era peak. The deal, which follows months of on-again, off-again negotiations, is being financed partly through an internal fundraising round of approximately Rs 375 crore from existing backers including Temasek, a common investor in both companies. The consolidation reflects broader pressure on India's online learning platforms as post-COVID enrolment normalised and profitability proved elusive. The combined entity would position UpGrad as India's dominant working-professional upskilling platform.

item.title: India's Major IT Firms Record Rising Revenue Per Employee as AI and Automation Drive Productivity Shift
item.description: India's top IT companies — including TCS, Infosys, HCLTech, and Tech Mahindra — have reported measurable increases in revenue generated per employee, a metric that signals a structural shift away from the traditional headcount-driven business model. Analysts attribute the gains to widespread adoption of AI coding assistants, automation of routine service tasks, and leaner project delivery pipelines. The trend suggests firms are extracting more value from existing workforces rather than scaling headcount proportionally with revenue. This marks one of the clearest financial confirmations yet that AI-led productivity is reshaping how India's $250-billion IT industry operates.

item.title: GalaxEye Launches World's First OptoSAR Satellite — India's Largest Private Space Payload Reaches Orbit
item.description: Indian deep-tech startup GalaxEye successfully launched Mission Drishti aboard a SpaceX rocket, making it the world's first satellite to combine electro-optical and synthetic aperture radar (OptoSAR) sensors in a single 190-kilogram platform — the largest satellite ever built by an Indian private company. The satellite is designed to capture high-quality Earth observation data regardless of weather or lighting conditions, overcoming limitations of conventional single-sensor systems. Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly hailed the launch as a landmark achievement for India's private space sector. GalaxEye expects to begin commercial data sales within eight weeks, with defence and security agencies anticipated as anchor customers.

item.title: MobiKwik Secures NBFC Licence From RBI, Launches Own Lending Subsidiary to Move Beyond Distribution
item.description: Digital payments and financial services platform MobiKwik has received a Non-Banking Financial Company licence from the Reserve Bank of India, allowing it to launch its own lending subsidiary, MobiKwik Financial Services Private Limited, and move from being a lending distributor to a direct lender. The NBFC licence is a significant regulatory milestone that gives MobiKwik control over its own credit products, pricing, and underwriting rather than acting as a pass-through for partner NBFCs. This transition is expected to improve unit economics and enable the platform to offer more competitive loan products to its user base of tens of millions of Indians.

item.title: Snabbit Raises $56M in Six Months After Last Round as Instant Home Services Race Intensifies in India
item.description: On-demand home services startup Snabbit has raised $56 million in a new round co-led by Susquehanna Venture Capital, Mirae Asset Venture Investments, and Bertelsmann India Investments, bringing its total capital raised to $112 million in under a year. The rapid successive fundraising reflects intensifying investor interest in India's instant home services category, where Snabbit competes to connect urban households with vetted domestic help on short notice. The company plans to use the capital to expand city coverage and deepen its service category range.

item.title: HyugaLife Raises Rs 100 Crore Series A to Scale AI Personalisation and Dark Store Network Across India
item.description: Health and wellness e-commerce platform HyugaLife has closed a Rs 100 crore Series A round led by IvyCap Ventures, which it will deploy to strengthen its AI-driven personalisation engine, expand its dark store fulfilment network, and open offline retail touchpoints. The company uses AI to match customers with personalised health product recommendations based on lifestyle data, aiming to compete in India's rapidly growing wellness commerce segment. The funding positions HyugaLife to scale beyond its current urban customer base into Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets.

item.title: Magellanic Cloud and Rayonix Tech Form Rs 100-Crore JV With Israel's Xtend to Make Drones in India
item.description: Indian technology firms Magellanic Cloud and Rayonix Tech have announced a Rs 100-crore joint venture with Israeli drone technology company Xtend to manufacture advanced unmanned aerial vehicles in India. The JV aims to meet India's growing demand for sophisticated drones, with the first production-ready drone sets expected within four to six months. The initiative aligns with India's Make in India push for defence and dual-use technology self-reliance, reducing dependence on imported UAV systems.

item.title: Sahamati Raises Rs 50 Crore to Deepen India's Account Aggregator Ecosystem
item.description: Sahamati, the industry alliance backing India's Account Aggregator financial data-sharing framework, has raised Rs 50 crore from financial sector entities to strengthen its technical and policy infrastructure. The capital will be used to deepen ecosystem participation among banks, insurers, and fintech players who use the AA framework to enable consent-based financial data sharing for millions of Indians. The Account Aggregator system is a foundational piece of India's Digital Public Infrastructure and underpins credit access for underserved borrowers.

item.title: Paytring Uses OpenAI Models to Fix Payment Chaos for Indian Merchants — Founder Explains How
item.description: Bengaluru-based fintech startup Paytring has built a payment orchestration layer for Indian merchants that uses OpenAI's language models to improve transaction success rates and simplify checkout operations. Founder Debal Chakraborty explains that AI is used to route payments intelligently across multiple gateways, reducing failures that cost merchants revenue on every failed transaction. The startup addresses a gap in India's booming digital payments ecosystem where checkout friction remains a persistent problem for small and mid-sized businesses.

item.title: India's Content Takedown Rules Under Scrutiny: Experts Warn of Expanding Powers With No Transparency
item.description: A MediaNama discussion surfaced expert warnings that India's content-blocking legal framework is being expanded through draft IT Rules in ways that are largely hidden from public view, with experts saying what is not disclosed may be more consequential than what is. Former MeitY official Rakesh Maheshwari and former Meta public policy manager Snehashish Ghosh traced the origins of the three-hour content takedown mandate to the 2019 election code of ethics, revealing how an emergency electoral measure has been normalised into permanent regulatory architecture. Panellists warned that the lack of transparency in how blocking decisions are made leaves citizens and platforms with no meaningful redress.

item.title: India's Draft IT Rules Trigger Free Speech Fears as IDC Gains Powers to Block Online Content
item.description: The Hindu's editorial analysis of India's proposed IT Rules amendments warns that the draft departs from existing Supreme Court rulings and consolidates content-blocking authority in the executive, raising the risk of digital overreach. The piece highlights how the proposed Inter-Departmental Committee structure lacks judicial checks, giving bureaucrats power to restrict online speech without transparency or appeal mechanisms. Legal experts cited in the article argue the rules conflict with constitutional free speech protections.

item.title: Experts Warn MeitY's Draft IT Rules Give Executive Power to Issue Binding AI Advisories, Bypassing Parliament
item.description: Legal and policy experts at a MediaNama event raised serious alarms over proposed Rule 3(4) in India's draft IT Rules amendments, which they say allows MeitY to issue binding advisories, guidelines, and standard operating procedures without parliamentary oversight or judicial review. Critics argue the provision effectively hands the executive branch unchecked authority to shape what speech is permissible online, with no mandatory transparency mechanism. The concern is compounded by separate warnings about an Inter-Departmental Committee being granted expansive powers to act as 'judge, jury, and executioner' over online content.

item.title: MeitY Secretary Confirms India in Direct Talks With Anthropic Over Mythos Cybersecurity Threat
item.description: India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Secretary S. Krishnan confirmed the Union government is in direct talks with Anthropic regarding concerns over the Mythos AI model, describing AI's impact on cybersecurity as a 'very real threat' that has materialised 'in very real terms.' The development signals the Indian government's escalating concern about advanced AI capabilities posing risks to national digital infrastructure. This is the first confirmed high-level bilateral engagement between MeitY and Anthropic specifically on the Mythos vulnerability.
